name: 38764-loradecode-qwen38b-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), sm90.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: Qwen3ForCausalLM, 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 query / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, max_position_embeddings 40960, bf16, ~16.4 GB of weights.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=1, bounded at 60 requests with a 1800 s safety cap, warmup the first 15% by completion, cooldown the last 10%. One stream is the declared operating point; do not walk it up, and do not lower the warmup.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, `request_format: plain`. Prompt exactly 64 tokens and output exactly 512 (fixed length, so the backend forces ignore_eos), temperature 0.0, static seed 38764.
purpose: A single-user long-form writing assistant on one H100, turning short prompts into 512-token answers with an 8B model.
launch:
# ENGINE: commit 3dc01ef352726e20b8a2e7c8430ae4544b7bb284 (`git describe --tags` =
# v0.18.2rc0-12-g3dc01ef352) -- a commit, not a release. The interpreter that holds it, and the
# hardware seal, live in configs/env.yaml, which is per-machine and NOT portable.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B

# REQUIRED BY THE SETUP: every request is served through one LoRA adapter. WHICH adapter is
# declared client-side, in scenario.json `spec.backend.lora_modules`, because the engine is driven
# in-process and `--lora-modules` is API-server surface that AsyncEngineArgs will not take.
enable-lora: true
max-lora-rank: 8
max-loras: 1

tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 40960
enable-prefix-caching: false

# This engine's own defaults, written down so they cannot drift. Neither scheduler bound binds at
# one request in flight.
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
max-num-seqs: 128
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
